title: Yamagata Prefecture
dek: Castle ruins, a 1,015-step mountain temple, and a gas-lit onsen village reached by a bus that only runs a few times a day.
verified: ⚠ Draft — Pass A (canonical/verified) + Pass B (local/authentic) + reconciliation completed 2026-08-28 for the Oct 20–23, 2026 trip. The anchor transfer (Oishida Station → Ginzan Onsen bus) is verified against the operator's own site, which publishes a separate timetable for its Apr 1 – Oct 24 and Dec 1 – Mar 31 seasons — the April–October table is the one covering these dates. Re-check before travel: the day's last inbound bus into Ginzan Onsen (the operator's 18:21 is the last bus OUT of the village, not the last one in), Risshaku-ji's closing time (the temple publishes hours for April–September and December–March only, and this trip falls in the unpublished October gap), Ginzan Onsen ryokan availability (a real booking-window risk — see Plan → Booking checklist), the Ginzan Onsen gas-lamp lighting time (lit at dusk; no exact time is published), JR fares and the Tsubasa reservation rule (JR East's own fare and timetable pages could not be reached during research), the Bunshokan assembly-hall reopening (targeted end of Sept 2026), the 2026 autumn foliage forecast (publishes from September), and whether a 2026 autumn/winter Ginzan Onsen vehicle-restriction window is announced (last year's dates weren't published until shortly before the season). Offline verify + networked verify have not run yet.

entry.visa: Visa-free entry for short-term tourism — commonly cited as up to 90 days under Japan's general visa-exemption framework. No pre-arrival electronic authorization (the proposed "JESTA" system) is required for 2026 travel; it is not scheduled to launch before Japan's 2028 fiscal year at the earliest.
entry.note: ASSUMED passport — the traveler party's passport countries were not stated in intake. This entry rests on Japan's national tourism organization, which states the 90-day tourism exemption and that Visit Japan Web registration is optional rather than required. ⚠ The definitive country-by-country list is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs', which could not be reached during research — re-confirm at mofa.go.jp, and update this once every traveler's actual passport country is known.
